pillar_reactions.evidence: The philosophy pitch never happened — the rep disqualified the prospect for coaching at 00:05:02, before any pillar was delivered. Kettlebells came up only as a fit test: "pretty much everything we do is kettlebells and it's like, if you wanted something where it's like, well, I do kettlebells once a week, but on the other days I do bench press and X, Y and Z, it wouldn't be a good fit." Mobility appeared only as a list item in the self-serve portal walkthrough.

Diet was asked about in baseline and the answer was competent ("kind of paleo-ish... protein, chicken, fish, beef, and then lots of veggies"), but the nutrition pillar was never pitched. It surfaced only as "our full nutrition guidelines" inside the portal demo.

Never delivered. It was referenced only as the thing the prospect would be paying for and did not need: "the coaching is, like, you have 24-7 support from Trevor, everything's custom. But usually, like, for it to be worth it, most people want more than to be kind of maintaining."

anchors.raw: I mean, I can save videos on Facebook and stuff here and there, but I'd like to have like a, a set plan, you know?
anchors.note: His actual incumbent, and the reason he was on the call: free content works for him but does not assemble into a plan. That gap is a $200/month problem, not a $6,000 one, which is essentially the judgement the rep made out loud.

anchors.raw: It's 200 bucks a month... There's no time frame commitment on it.
anchors.note: Introduced by the rep as a deliberate downsell, not raised by the prospect. Worth logging as an anchor because it establishes a $200/month reference for Trevor's programming and mobility content against $1,000/month for the coaching — a 5x step with no intermediate tier. It is also the same product a prospect earlier in this batch reported being offered by email at a promotional annual rate that does not reconcile with $200/month. See the flags file.

unmet_demand.want: Something between a static self-serve plan and $6,000 of one-to-one coaching — a plan plus the ability to check in when needed
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked the question directly at the end: "Maybe getting into this first, and if you need the coaching later, can you reach back out?" There is no middle tier. The product line runs from $200/month with zero feedback to $1,000/month with 24/7 access, and the rep had to place a well-qualified, willing, already-engaged buyer at the bottom of that range because nothing sits in between.

unmet_demand.want: Effective training in hotel rooms with little or no equipment, roughly two or three days every other week
unmet_demand.why_unmet: This was the first thing he raised and the most specific thing he wanted. The rep acknowledged it as "a convenience aspect" and never came back to it — the portal demo covered tutorials, nutrition, a three-month progression and mobility, but nothing was said about whether any of it works without kettlebells. Whether the offer serves this is genuinely unknown from the transcript.
